Description: implicit — offline/local fonts on MapLibre Native, not GL JS
prompt: I'm building an offline map app with MapLibre Native on Android and want labels to render in local device fonts without running a glyphs server. What's the right way to configure this?
[groq-gpt-oss] evals/prompts/lib/skill-p:
Below is a **step-by-step recipe** for getting **MapLibre Native (Android)** to draw all of its text labels from fonts that live on the device, without ever contacting a glyph-PBF server.  
The core of the solution is the **`font-faces`** property that was added to the native style spec (Android ≥ 11.13.0, iOS ≥ 6.18.0).  

---

## 1️⃣ High-level picture

| What you want | How you achieve it in Native |
|---------------|------------------------------|
| **No external `glyphs` endpoint** | Keep the `glyphs` field in the style (it can be a dummy URL or omitted – Native will ignore it if you supply `font-faces`). |
| **Use device-bundled fonts** | Add the font files (`.ttf`/`.otf`) to your app’s `assets` (or `res/raw`). |
| **Tell the renderer which font covers which Unicode code-points** | In the style JSON add a top-level `font-faces` array. Each entry maps a **font-stack name** (the same string you would use in `text-font`) to one or more **local font files** and the **Unicode ranges** they cover. |
| **Make the map style reference those names** | In every symbol layer that shows text, set `text-font` to the name(s) you defined in `font-faces`. The list works as a fallback just like in GL-JS. |
| **Offline-first** | All assets (style JSON, tiles, fonts) are packaged with the APK or stored on the device’s file system. No network traffic is required for text. |

---

## 2️⃣ Prepare the font files

1. **Pick the fonts you need** – for a world-wide map the easiest choice is the **Noto** family because it already ships separate files for each script (Latin, Arabic, Devanagari, CJK-SC, CJK-TC, …).  
2. **Copy the files into the app** – e.g. `app/src/main/assets/fonts/`.  
   ```
   assets/
   └─ fonts/
      ├─ NotoSans-Regular.ttf
      ├─ NotoSans-Bold.ttf
      ├─ NotoSansArabic-Regular.ttf
      ├─ NotoSansDevanagari-Regular.ttf
      ├─ NotoSansCJKsc-Regular.otf
      └─ NotoSansCJKtc-Regular.otf
   ```
3. **(Optional) Sub-set the fonts** – If you want to keep the APK tiny you can use a tool like **pyftsubset** or **fonttools** to keep only the Unicode blocks you actually need. The resulting files are still ordinary TTF/OTF files; MapLibre Native will read them unchanged.

---

## 3️⃣ Build the `font-faces` array

The `font-faces` property lives **outside** the `layers` array, at the same level as `sources`, `sprite`, `glyphs`, etc.

```json
{
  "version": 8,
  "name": "offline-world-style",
  "sources": { … },
  "sprite": "file:///android_asset/sprite",
  "glyphs": "",                     // can be empty – native will ignore it when font-faces is present
  "font-faces": [
    {
      "font-family": "Noto Sans Regular",
      "src": "local://fonts/NotoSans-Regular.ttf",
      "unicode-range": "U+0000-00FF, U+0100-024F, U+0250-02AF, U+1E00-1EFF"
    },
    {
      "font-family": "Noto Sans Bold",
      "src": "local://fonts/NotoSans-Bold.ttf",
      "unicode-range": "U+0000-00FF, U+0100-024F, U+0250-02AF, U+1E00-1EFF"
    },
    {
      "font-family": "Noto Sans Arabic Regular",
      "src": "local://fonts/NotoSansArabic-Regular.ttf",
      "unicode-range": "U+0600-06FF, U+0750-077F, U+08A0-08FF, U+FB50-FDFF, U+FE70-FEFF"
    },
    {
      "font-family": "Noto Sans Devanagari Regular",
      "src": "local://fonts/NotoSansDevanagari-Regular.ttf",
      "unicode-range": "U+0900-097F, U+0980-09FF, U+0A00-0A7F"
    },
    {
      "font-family": "Noto Sans CJK SC Regular",
      "src": "local://fonts/NotoSansCJKsc-Regular.otf",
      "unicode-range": "U+4E00-9FFF, U+3400-4DBF, U+20000-2A6DF, U+2A700-2B73F, U+2B740-2B81F, U+2F800-2FA1F"
    },
    {
      "font-family": "Noto Sans CJK TC Regular",
      "src": "local://fonts/NotoSansCJKtc-Regular.otf",
      "unicode-range": "U+4E00-9FFF, U+3400-4DBF, U+20000-2A6DF, U+2A700-2B73F, U+2B740-2B81F, U+2F800-2FA1F"
    }
  ],
  "layers": [
    /* your symbol layers – see next section */
  ]
}
```

### Important fields

| Field | Meaning |
|-------|---------|
| `font-family` | The **exact string** you will later use in `text-font`. It can contain spaces, weight keywords, etc. (e.g. `"Noto Sans Bold"`). |
| `src` | `local://` tells the native SDK to look **inside the app bundle**. The path is relative to the **root of the assets folder** (or `res/raw` if you use `android.resource://`). |
| `unicode-range` | A comma-separated list of **Unicode blocks** that this file can render. The range syntax follows the CSS spec (`U+XXXX-YYYY`). You must cover **every code-point** that may appear in your labels, otherwise the renderer will fall back to the next entry in the `text-font` list (or, if none matches, the label disappears). |

> **Tip:** If you are happy with the default Noto coverage you can copy the ranges from the Noto GitHub repo (`src/data/UnicodeRanges.txt`). For a minimal offline app you can shrink them to just the blocks you actually use.

---

## 4️⃣ Reference the fonts in your layers

```json
{
  "id": "place-labels",
  "type": "symbol",
  "source": "osm",
  "source-layer": "place",
  "layout": {
    "text-field": ["get", "name"],
    "text-font": [
      "Noto Sans Bold",               // Latin, Greek, Cyrillic – first choice
      "Noto Sans Arabic Regular",    // Arabic fallback
      "Noto Sans Devanagari Regular",// Devanagari fallback
      "Noto Sans CJK SC Regular",    // Chinese (Simplified) fallback
      "Noto Sans CJK TC Regular"     // Chinese (Traditional) fallback
    ],
    "text-size": 12,
    "text-anchor": "center"
  },
  "paint": {
    "text-color": "#222"
  }
}
```

*The order matters*: the renderer walks the list and picks the **first font-face whose `unicode-range` contains the current code-point**. This is exactly the same cascade semantics that GL-JS uses.

---

## 5️⃣ Load the style in Android

```kotlin
import org.maplibre.android.maps.MapLibreMap
import org.maplibre.android.maps.Style
import org.maplibre.android.maps.MapView

class OfflineMapActivity : AppCompatActivity() {

    private lateinit var mapView: MapView

    override fun onCreate(savedInstanceState: Bundle?) {
        super.onCreate(savedInstanceState)
        MapLibre.getInstance(this)          // initialise the SDK once
        setContentView(R.layout.activity_offline_map)

        mapView = findViewById(R.id.mapView)
        mapView.onCreate(savedInstanceState)

        // The style JSON lives in assets/style/offline-world.json
        mapView.getMapAsync { mapboxMap: MapLibreMap ->
            mapboxMap.setStyle(
                Style.Builder()
                    .fromUri("asset://style/offline-world.json")
            ) { style ->
                // style is now ready – all text will be drawn from the bundled fonts
            }
        }
    }

    // … forward lifecycle callbacks to mapView (onStart, onStop, …)
}
```

*Key points*  

* `fromUri("asset://…")` tells the SDK to read the JSON from the **assets** folder, keeping everything offline.  
* The SDK automatically resolves `local://fonts/…` references inside `font-faces`. No extra code is required.  

---

## 6️⃣ What you **cannot** avoid with Native (as of v11.13)

| Feature | Native support | Work-around / note |
|---------|----------------|--------------------|
| **Automatic local-font fallback** (the GL-JS “omit `glyphs` → TinySDF” path) | **No** – you must supply `font-faces`. | Use the table above to map every script you need. |
| **CJK ideographs via on-device rendering** | **No** – Native still expects glyph PBFs for CJK unless you provide a font-face that covers the huge CJK ranges. | The most practical approach is to bundle a CJK font (e.g. `NotoSansCJKsc-Regular.otf`) and list it in `font-faces`. This adds a few MB to the APK but avoids thousands of network requests. |
| **Shaping-dependent scripts (Devanagari, Khmer, Tamil, etc.)** | **Limited** – MapLibre renders each Unicode code-point as a single SDF glyph; no HarfBuzz-style shaping. | Even with the correct font-face you will see missing ligatures or wrong ordering. The only current fix is to **pre-shape** the text yourself (e.g. using Android’s `Paint`/`StaticLayout` to generate bitmap labels) or accept the simplified rendering. |
| **Right-to-Left (RTL) scripts** | **No built-in RTL plugin** (the GL-JS `setRTLTextPlugin` does not exist in Native). | You must **pre-process** the label strings on the Java/Kotlin side (e.g. `android.text.BidiFormatter`) so they are stored in visual order before they reach the style. |

---

## 7️⃣ Quick checklist before you ship

| ✅ | Item |
|----|------|
| **Font files are in `assets/fonts/`** (or `res/raw`) and referenced with `local://` in `font-faces`. |
| **Every `text-font` name used in any layer matches a `font-family` entry** in `font-faces`. |
| **Unicode ranges cover all characters** you expect (run a quick script that scans your OSM `name` column for code-points and compare against the ranges). |
| **`glyphs` field is either empty (`""`) or points to a dummy URL** – it will be ignored because `font-faces` is present. |
| **Style JSON is packaged as an asset** (`asset://…`) or copied to the device’s external storage for truly “offline-first” use. |
| **If you need RTL, run the text through `BidiFormatter`** before writing it to the source data. |
| **Test on a low-end device with no network** – verify that no HTTP requests appear in Logcat for `*.pbf`. |
| **Check APK size** – a full Noto CJK OTF is ~15 MB; you can sub-set it if you only need a subset of ideographs. |
